request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched" figure: the due-totals of everyone the signed-in user watches, added up. It reads 0.00 when they watch no one. `bin/e2e` ran all 4 tests in the spec and they passed.

**What changed:** only `src/main/frontend/features/counters/HeaderCounters.tsx`. No server or database changes were needed, because the app already stored watches and had an endpoint to fetch them.

**How it works:**
- It takes the sheet's watches and keeps only the signed-in user's.
- Each watched person's due-total is worked out the same way as their own due figure elsewhere on the screen, then the totals are added up. A watched person with no figure is skipped.
- It's shown as `watched-due-total`, after "My reviews" in the counters line.
- Nothing new is written to the audit file, since the spec expects no audit record for this.
